analysis.title: The Oil Gusher: Long-term oil demand: Peak to plateau?
key_insights: BofA sees long-term oil demand peaking around 2030 at about 108mb/d, then declining to under 100mb/d by 2040 and under 90mb/d by 2050, a long plateau rather than a sharp peak.
All base case outlooks except OPEC show roughly flat demand of about 102-106mb/d into 2030. OPEC expects 113mb/d in 2030 and 124.1mb/d in 2050 in its reference case.

OPEC's most bearish scenario sits above every other agency's base case. BofA questions whether this is wishful thinking or an attempt to impose discipline on members seeking to recover market share once Hormuz and new export pipelines allow flows to recover.

TotalEnergies' 2026 Energy Outlook calls Net Zero 2050 beyond reach. Its Trends base case implies 2.5-2.8C of warming by 2100, with oil demand plateauing near current levels into 2030 and falling to 93mb/d by 2050.

The IEA WEO 2026 has five scenarios. STEPS levels off at 103mb/d around 2030, CPS reaches 106mb/d in 2035 and 114mb/d in 2050, ARC falls to 85mb/d by 2050, and NZE falls to 28mb/d. All scenarios exceed 1.5C of warming by 2050.

Road transport is the key driver of demand decline. Under STEPS road oil demand falls about 5% by 2035, while petchem rises 17% and aviation 25%. OPEC instead sees about 6mb/d of road demand growth to 2050.

COP31 draft '35x35' targets electricity at 35% of final energy consumption by 2035, backed by more than 75 countries. The fossil fuel phase-out language and finance-alignment language were dropped or diluted, and methane language was softened.

BofA highlights TTE's Integrated Power portfolio, with FCF breakeven expected in 2026, positive FCF in 2027 and 12% ROACE by 2030. This lowers TTE's oil price breakeven as Brent normalises toward BofA's $60-80/bbl mid-cycle.

Back-solved valuations show European Big Oils discount an average long-term Brent of about $66/bbl. TTE and Galp are lowest at under $45/bbl, with Repsol and OMV at the high end. BofA uses $70/bbl from 2028.
European Big Oils show average organic FCF yield of 15.8% in 2026, falling to 10.7% in 2027 and 9.1% in 2028. Aggregate 2026 organic FCF post distributions is $77bn and FCF surplus is $58bn.
BP has the highest gearing of the group, about 30% on BofA's definition at YE26 versus about 15% for TTE and Shell. Repsol is closest to sub-investment grade on credit ratings.
Consensus has revised 2026 net income up 197% on average versus share prices up 40% YTD. BofA estimates are 2% ahead of consensus on 2026 net income, organic CFFO and EBITDA.

Commodity backdrop: Brent about $92/bbl, TTF about EUR82/MWh, European gas storage 70% full versus 81% a year ago, European refining margin about $24/bbl, and US crude cover about 25 days, below the five-year average.

Sector valuation: SXEP dividend and FCF yields sit above the broader SXXP. 75% of European Big Oils trade above their 10-year average FCF yield, and none trade above their 10-year average dividend yield.

market_movers.rationale: The share price implies under $45/bbl long-term Brent, helped by Renewables valued at over $50bn NPV. The Integrated Power FCF inflection lowers breakevens.
Galp is Buy rated and its share price discounts under $45/bbl long-term Brent.
BP has the highest gearing at about 30% on BofA's definition, and the report calls it an outlier among peers.
Equinor's FCF yield is the most sensitive to oil and gas prices, and its methane and CCS positioning is strong.
Shell is Neutral in the coverage cluster.
Eni is Neutral in the coverage cluster.
Repsol is Underperform and is the closest to sub-investment grade on credit ratings.

sector_views.rationale: Big Oils discount about $66/bbl long-term Brent against BofA's $60-80/bbl mid-cycle, with high 2026 FCF yields falling in 2027.
COP31 electrification momentum favours TTE's Integrated Power portfolio, whose FCF is inflecting.

earnings_insights: BofA 2026 estimates are 2% ahead of Visible Alpha consensus on net income, organic CFFO and EBITDA, as forecasts, not reported figures.
BofA 2026 organic FCF is 7% ahead of consensus, with 2027 and 2028 FCF 9% and 20% ahead (BofA estimates versus Visible Alpha consensus).
At strip prices BofA 2026 net income and organic CFFO are in line with consensus, as estimates.
Aggregate 2026 organic FCF pre-distributions is $144bn (BofA estimate), with $35.8bn dividends and $31.1bn buybacks.
Visible Alpha consensus 2026 net income has been revised up 197% on average YTD, versus a 40% average share price gain.
Upcoming results: Vallourec 3Q26 on 20 Nov, Equinor 3 Feb, OMV and Shell 4 Feb, TotalEnergies 10 Feb, Neste 10 Feb.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Spot level is above BofA's $60-80/bbl mid-cycle range, with 2026 forecast above $90/bbl.
Assumes Middle East de-escalation, and the range is unchanged.
A tight European gas market, with TTF at a 172% implied slope to Brent.
Storage is 11pp below last year, which supports gas prices.
Diesel crack about $57/bbl and kerosene crack about $71/bbl.
A plateau followed by a gradual decline of about 1% CAGR.

risk_factors: Sharp moves in refining margins, oil and gas prices and the USD.
Government intervention, regulation, expropriation, project execution and litigation risks.
If OPEC's no-peak view proves right, long-term oil prices could be higher than BofA assumes. If demand peaks sooner, they would be lower.
Further Hormuz disruption or a faster return of flows would swing Brent and market share dynamics.
BP gearing and the credit rating spread, with Repsol closest to sub-investment grade.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 shows Brent price priced into each Big Oil share, with and without Renewables NPV, against the $60-80/bbl range. TTE is below $45/bbl and the average is about $66/bbl.
Exhibit 4 compares base case oil demand projections by agency to 2050, with OPEC showing no peak.
Exhibit 28 states Brent trades at about $92/bbl.
Exhibit 38 states European gas storage is 70% full versus 81% last year.
vol_and_positioning: 75% of European Big Oils trade above their 10-year average FCF yields, while none are above 10-year average dividend yields.
Share price performance: TotalEnergies was the best Big Oil over the last week and month, and Repsol is the best YTD.
geopolitical: Strait of Hormuz disruption and the Middle East conflict. IEA scenarios assume Gulf export constraints ease into 2027 and unimpeded transit by end-2027.
COP31 negotiations, with the final communique expected over the weekend.
The IEA Low Hormuz Case cuts oil transiting Hormuz to about 2mb/d in 2035 from 20mb/d in STEPS, mainly via bypass pipelines.
Russian LNG sanctions are referenced in the recent research list as a factor for Europe's gas winter.
cross_bank_references: BP's 2025 edition is the most bearish base case for 2050 oil demand, at about 83mb/d.
In line with BofA estimates, the IEA STEPS scenario sees oil demand peaking by the end of the decade.

tension_points.bull_case: OPEC sees demand growing to 113mb/d by 2030 and 124.1mb/d by 2050, driven by road transport and developing economies.
tension_points.bear_case: BofA, the IEA, TTE and BP see a plateau or peak around 2030, with road demand falling as EVs spread and electrification accelerates.
tension_points.what_invalidates: OPEC's road growth thesis would fail if the IEA's STEPS projection of road oil demand down about 5% by 2035 materialises.

theme_stances.key_argument: Base cases show long plateaus rather than sharp peaks, with little hope for near-term growth outside OPEC.
theme_stances.evidence: instead of sharp peaks, base cases see long plateaus

theme_stances.key_argument: OPEC's no-peak forecast may be wishful thinking or an effort to instil discipline among members.
theme_stances.evidence: wishful thinking or an attempt at instilling discipline among cartel members

theme_stances.key_argument: COP31 electrification policy favours TTE's Integrated Power, whose FCF inflection cuts oil price breakeven.
